claims.text: The driver never held the pickup point for the minimum waiting period in any continuous stretch. On his own trace the two spells inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup are 170 seconds (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 seconds (18:49:35 to 18:52:40), against the 300 second minimum for the zone class. His longest single hold is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short, and neither spell reaches five minutes. That is exactly the rider's complaint, in her own words, that the car never stayed five minutes in one place before the driver cancelled and charged her SGD 4.00.

The charge also fails POL-NS-01(d), which makes the fee chargeable only where the trip is terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. Measured from the start of the driver's final in-geofence hold at 18:49:35, a continuous 300 second dwell would not have elapsed until 18:54:35, yet the trip record shows the driver cancelling at 18:52:45 - 110 seconds early. The cancellation therefore lands inside the waiting period the fee is supposed to purchase, not after it.

POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) both run off the trace, not off the driver's tap. Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 pickup geofence at or before the 18:44:30 'arrived' event, and limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the event. The trace's in-geofence intervals begin only at 18:44:45, fifteen seconds after the marker, so the record does not establish an in-geofence position at the moment the driver marked arrived, and the waiting clock cannot be started earlier than 18:44:45 on this evidence.

The only route to 300 seconds on this record is the summing allowed by POL-NS-06(i). The kerb-restriction advisory on the file does one thing: it permits the two in-geofence spells to be added together. It does not convert the 120 seconds the car spent away from the bay - 18:47:35 to 18:49:35, when the driver's own trace puts the vehicle up to 179 m from the pin - into waiting time, and the driver's own chat message at 18:47:50 ('i go one round and come back same place ah') is his admission that he left. Even taking the accumulated figure at its highest, the driver clears the 300 second minimum by only 55 seconds, on a trace whose longest undisturbed hold is 185 seconds. The rider is asked to pay for a continuous wait that was never held.

POL-NS-06 is strict about the waiting period: where the effective dwell falls short, the fee is refunded to the rider in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The driver's account that the rider said she was coming down at 6.46 and never came cannot therefore save the charge - the fee is earned by the dwell, not by the rider's conduct - and the contested SGD 4.00 should be returned in full to the filing rider under POL-GEN-03.

claims.text: The driver's own trace contains 40 qualifying position fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius fixed for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, delivered as two continuous in-geofence holds of 18 fixes (18:44:45-18:47:35) and 20 fixes (18:49:35-18:52:40). POL-NS-02 requires only three consecutive in-radius fixes with 25 m accuracy or better, so the driver is deemed to have ARRIVED at the ION Orchard PHV bay on the platform's own numbers, not on his say-so.

The rider's core complaint is that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place.' That is true of the longest single hold (185 seconds), and it is precisely the case POL-NS-06(i) was written for: dwell may be accumulated across separate in-geofence intervals where the driver never went more than 300 m from the pin AND a traffic advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION covered the pickup road during the waiting period. Here the LTA advisory is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane 17:00-20:00 on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn between Paterson Rd and Bideford Rd), its geometry contains the pickup point and its window covers the whole wait, and the driver's furthest point during the loop was 179.0 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. The effective dwell is therefore 170 + 185 = 355 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum, the derived shortfall is negative (-55 s), and POL-NS-06's full-refund route is not triggered.

The chat independently corroborates the loop and its cause. At 18:47:50 — exactly when the trace shows the driver leaving the bay at 18:47:35 to begin the 120 second excursion — he wrote 'boss the marshal make me move, bus lane until 8pm. i go one round and come back same place ah'. The trace shows him back at the same bay by 18:49:35. The absence from the kerb was compliance with a lawfully enforced bus lane, not abandonment of the pickup, which is the situation POL-NS-06(i) exists to stop penalising.

All four POL-NS-01 limbs are made out on this record. (a) The trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30. (b) The trace places the driver in the pickup geofence with 40 qualifying fixes. (c) The effective in-geofence dwell under POL-NS-06(i) is 355 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the 'arrived' tap. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, no boarding event and no started_at. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces that, so the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is chargeable as itemised.

Taking the point against the driver at its highest — that the 18:44:30 'arrived' tap preceded the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45 by 15 seconds — POL-NS-05 still does not defeat the fee. Its trigger is a fix more than 300 m from the pin or travel at 15 km/h or above at the marker; more importantly limb (iii) says expressly that a marker which is merely early is not a technicality that voids an otherwise good fee, because the waiting clock is simply recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and on that recomputed basis the dwell (355 seconds accumulated) still meets the LARGE_VENUE minimum. POL-NS-01 therefore governs the outcome.

POL-NS-04 cannot exculpate the rider on either limb. Limb (b) fails: the rider's only message in the waiting window is MSG-00214-003 at 18:46:20 ('ok coming down now'), and the driver answered it in the chat at 18:47:50 — 90 seconds later, inside the 120 second limit — so the no-reply condition is not met and the clause does not apply. Limb (c) fails affirmatively as well: the rider_track records 70 fixes, every one of them outside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider presence radius (minimum 690.7 m, mean 702.7 m from the pin), giving rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0.

The rider's narrative — 'I was watching the app the whole time' and 'coming down now' — is contradicted by his own device. His track runs 70 fixes from 18:44:00 to 18:52:40, all at 0.0 km/h, pinned between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin for the entire window. At 18:46:20 he told the driver he was coming down; six minutes later he had moved not at all. That is the RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation reason code made out on the rider's own telemetry, and it is why the fee was charged.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 gives the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, with the 20 percent platform service fee retained. The anti-farming guard does not bite: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, far below 0.08. Both limbs are required and neither is met, so compensation is payable and no escalation arises under POL-NS-09.

The amount charged is correct and gives the rider no route to even a partial refund. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) — and the two dimensions agree, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and there is no fare defect for the rider to exploit.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius; this driver's holds were inside it, so there is no wrong-entrance or wrong-block case to allocate. Its pin-ambiguity branch in limb (ii) is unavailable in any event because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more, so no platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent arises and the fee is not displaced.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.00 no-show cancellation fee stands, and the driver is paid $3.20 of it as compensation.

Arrival. The platform GPS trace places the driver inside the 120 m pickup geofence at the ION Orchard PHV bay with 40 qualifying fixes; the policy requires only three. So the driver had arrived (POL-NS-01(b), POL-NS-02). The rider's point that the 'arrived' tap at 18:44:30 was 15 seconds ahead of the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45 does not defeat the charge: a false marker requires the driver to have been either more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more at the marker, and neither is shown (POL-NS-05). A slightly early tap is expressly not a technicality that voids an otherwise good fee.

Waiting time. You are right, rider, that the car never stood still for five unbroken minutes — the two spells at the bay were 170 seconds (18:44:45-18:47:35) and 185 seconds (18:49:35-18:52:40). But POL-NS-06(i) expressly allows those separated spells to be added where a lawfully enforced kerb restriction made holding position impossible: the LTA advisory on file is a bus-lane / no-stopping restriction covering Orchard Road and Orchard Turn from 17:00 to 20:00, its geometry covers the pickup point, its window covers the whole wait, and the driver never went further than 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. Added together his in-geofence time is 355 seconds against the 300-second minimum for a large-venue pickup, so there is no shortfall and the waiting-period rule in POL-NS-06 does not return the fee. The 2-minute loop away from the bay (18:47:35-18:49:35) is not counted as waiting time; the driver's own message at 18:47:50 shows the marshal moved him on, not that he abandoned the pickup. On the accumulated basis the required waiting time was complete at 18:51:45, so the 18:52:45 cancellation came after it (POL-NS-01(d)).

The rider is not exonerated by POL-NS-04. The driver replied to her message within 90 seconds, inside the 120-second limit, so that clause does not apply regardless of content; and independently her own device sat 690-717 m from the pickup pin, outside the 150 m rider-presence radius, through the whole window.

Compensation and amount. POL-NS-07 gives the driver 80% of the $4.00 fee, i.e. $3.20, with 20% retained as platform fee. The anti-farming guard does not bite: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days is below the threshold of 4, and 2/118 is 0.017, far below 0.08, so both limbs fail and no escalation arises. The $4.00 charged also reconciles with the fee schedule — the greater of the $4.00 large-venue fee and the $4.00 RYDE_X tier fee — so there is no fare defect (POL-NS-08(d)). Profile facts other than the counters the policy names for this category (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d) were treated as background only and carry no weight.

Outcome: the rider's $4.00 charge is not refunded; the driver is paid $3.20. No referral is made, because no clause produces one on these facts (the arrival was genuine, so POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire).

To the rider and the driver.

OUTCOME: The SGD 4.00 no-show fee stands, and the driver is to be paid SGD 3.20 in compensation (80% of the fee; the platform retains the remaining 20%). The rider's challenge to the charge is not supported by the evidence.

For the RIDER. Your central point is that the car never stayed five minutes in one place, and on the raw holds that is correct: the trace shows two spells inside the 120 m large-venue pickup geofence, 170 seconds (6:44:45-6:47:35) and 185 seconds (6:49:35-6:52:40), and neither hold reaches the 300-second minimum on its own. But POL-NS-06(i) permits those two spells to be summed where the driver left and re-entered the arrival radius without ever travelling more than 300 m from the pin AND a kerb restriction covering the pickup road made holding the spot unlawful. Both conditions are met here: the driver's furthest point on the loop was 178.95 m from the pin (inside the 300 m leash), and the LTA advisory on file - Orchard Road / Orchard Turn full-day bus lane, 17:00-20:00, type KERB_RESTRICTION - covered the pickup road and the whole waiting window. Summed, the in-geofence time is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum. POL-NS-06's automatic full-refund route therefore does not fire, and the driver's chat message at 18:47:50 ('boss the marshal make me move, bus lane until 8pm. i go one round and come back same place ah'), sent exactly as the trace shows him leaving the bay, confirms the loop was compliance with an enforced bus lane rather than abandonment of the pickup.

Your two subsidiary arguments also fail. First, you say the 18:44:30 'arrived' tap is not supported because the trace's first in-geofence fix is at 18:44:45. The waiting clock under POL-NS-01(c) runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the tap, and the trace does place the driver in the geofence continuously from 18:44:45 across the whole attempt. The tap is not a false arrival on POL-NS-05's own test - at 18:44:30 the trace neither puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin nor shows him at 15 km/h or more - and an early or sloppy tap does not void a fee whose recomputed dwell is met. No false-arrival referral arises. Second, you say the cancellation at 18:52:45 came before a 300-second dwell could elapse. That measures the clock from the start of the final hold alone; with the two spells accumulated as POL-NS-06(i) requires, the required 300 seconds elapsed at about 18:51:45, and the cancellation at 18:52:45 is after that.

Separately, POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you. Your only coordinating message was at 18:46:20, and the driver replied at 18:47:50 - 90 seconds later, inside the 120-second limit - so limb (b) is not met; and your own rider_track shows 70 fixes, all stationary, between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pin, so limb (c)'s 150 m presence radius is affirmatively failed (rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0). Your 'coming down now' message at 18:46:20 is contradicted by your own device, which did not move.

For the DRIVER. All four POL-NS-01 limbs are made out: (a) the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30; (b) the trace places the driver inside the pickup geofence, with 40 qualifying fixes at 25 m accuracy or better; (c) the effective dwell, correctly accumulated under POL-NS-06(i), is 355 seconds against the 300-second minimum; and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event and no started_at. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces that. POL-NS-03 has no purchase at all: your holds were inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue outside it, and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill branch is unavailable. The SGD 4.00 charge reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule (the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X tier fee of 4.00), so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists.

Under POL-NS-07 you are entitled to 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, with the 20 percent platform service fee retained. The anti-farming guard does not apply: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, far below 0.08. Both limbs must be met and neither is, so compensation is paid and the fee stands.

Escalation and referrals. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence (the trace and the chat agree, and the rider's narrative is contradicted by the rider's own track); the same-party dispute counters are zero; the anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, not 3 or more; and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d). No clause produces a referral. Under POL-GEN-01 the profile fields were used only for the tests that name them (POL-NS-07), and no context-only field was used as a ground of decision.

Confidence. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts - the GPS trace, trip record, chat log, fare breakdown and LTA advisory - is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; I state 0.90 to reflect the single 15-second gap between the arrived tap and the first qualifying in-geofence fix, which does not change the outcome.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: the $4.00 no-show fee stands as charged, and the driver is paid $3.20 of it under POL-NS-07. Both money fields carry the same figure because that is the amount this ruling moves (POL-GEN-03); it is not a refund to the rider.

To the rider. Your description of the car moving about is factually correct, and I have not treated it as mistaken: the trace shows the driver holding the ION Orchard bay for 170 seconds (18:44:45-18:47:35), leaving for about two minutes, and holding it again for 185 seconds (18:49:35-18:52:40). He never stayed five unbroken minutes in one place. However, POL-NS-06(i) lets those two spells be added together where the driver left and re-entered the arrival radius without ever travelling more than 300 m from the pin AND a kerb restriction of the listed type was in force on the pickup road. Both conditions hold on the platform's own numbers: his furthest point during the loop was 179.0 m from the pin (inside the 300 m leash), and LTA's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01 (KERB_RESTRICTION, full-day bus lane on Orchard Road/Orchard Turn 17:00-20:00, geometry covering the pickup road and window covering the whole wait) means holding the kerb was not lawfully possible. That is the very thing the driver told you at 18:47:50 and what the marshal enforced. The effective dwell is therefore 170 + 185 = 355 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a surplus of 55 seconds. On your specific points: (i) your reading that the clock cannot start before the first in-geofence fix at 18:44:45 is accepted - POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying fix, not the 18:44:30 tap - but it does not change the result, because 355 seconds still clears 300; (ii) your point that a fresh 300 seconds from 18:49:35 would not have run by the 18:52:45 cancellation is right only if the earlier 170 seconds are discarded, and POL-NS-06(i) says they are summed, so the minimum was reached at about 18:51:45, before the cancellation; (iii) your point that the fee is earned by the waiting period and not by your conduct is correct as a principle, but the waiting period was served, so POL-NS-06's refund route is not engaged. POL-NS-04 does not help you either: the driver answered your 18:46:20 message at 18:47:50, inside the 120-second limit, so the no-reply condition fails, and your own trace places your device 690-717 m from the pin throughout, outside the 150 m large-venue presence radius. POL-NS-06 does not require a refund, and none is due.

To the driver. The fee is chargeable under POL-NS-01: an 'arrived' event exists (18:44:30); the trace places you inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius with 40 qualifying fixes; the effective dwell measured from the first qualifying fix is 355 seconds against the 300-second minimum; and the trip was terminated by you at 18:52:45 with no boarding event and reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, at or after the moment the minimum elapsed. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. POL-NS-03 does not apply because you were inside the arrival radius rather than outside it, and in any event registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill branch is unavailable. POL-NS-05 is not triggered: nothing places you more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above at the arrival timestamp, and the 15-second earliness of the tap is the harmless kind POL-NS-05(iii) describes, the clock simply being recomputed from 18:44:45. POL-NS-06 finds no shortfall. POL-NS-08 shows no impairment of any artifact that carries the decision: no clock skew (the arrival event sits within 5 seconds of a fix), no trace gap (100% coverage, maximum gap 0 seconds, 83 fixes), the chat numbering and count reconcile with trip_record.chat_message_count, and the $4.00 fee reconciles with the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. POL-NS-07 therefore pays you 80% of the fee, $3.20, with the residual $0.80 retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming guard does not bite: no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2/118 completed trips is 0.017 (below 0.08), so both limbs fail and no escalation arises under POL-NS-09. The profiles were used only as POL-GEN-01 permits - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d for the POL-NS-07 check - and no finding rests on any context-only field. No clause on this record produces a referral.

Both parties: the $4.00 no-show charge stands, and the driver is paid 80% of it ($3.20). Here is why, point by point.

RIDER — your main complaint, that the car kept moving and never held the bay for five minutes, is factually borne out by the GPS trace: the driver's two stops inside the 120 m ION Orchard pickup zone lasted 170 s (6.44.45–6.47.35pm) and 185 s (6.49.35–6.52.40pm), and his longest single stop was 185 s, not five minutes. But the policy does not ask for one continuous stop here. POL-NS-06(i) lets the two in-zone stops be added together where the driver never went more than 300 m from the pin and a kerb restriction made it unlawful to hold position. Both conditions are met: the LTA bus-lane advisory (no stopping 5–8pm on Orchard Road / Orchard Turn between Paterson Rd and Bideford Rd) covers the pickup road and the whole wait, and the driver's furthest point on his loop was 179 m from the pin. The effective wait is therefore 170 + 185 = 355 seconds, comfortably over the 300-second (5-minute) minimum for a large-venue pickup, and the derived shortfall is minus 55 seconds. Your argument that the 120 seconds away 'was not waiting' cannot be accepted — that gap is exactly what limb (i) exists to allow when the law forces the driver off the kerb, and the driver said so in the chat at 6.47.50pm. Your second point, that the 6.44.30pm 'arrived' tap came 15 seconds before the first in-zone fix at 6.44.45pm, also does not change the outcome: the marker is not a false arrival under POL-NS-05 (no fix over 300 m and no reading at 15 km/h or more at the marker), and in any event the waiting clock runs from the first qualifying in-zone fix, which still yields 355 seconds. Your third point, that the driver cancelled before the required dwell elapsed, fails once the stops are summed: 300 seconds of in-zone wait was reached at 6.51.45pm and the cancellation was at 6.52.45pm, so limb (d) is met.

RIDER — POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you. The driver answered your 'ok coming down now' message at 6.47.50pm, within 120 seconds, so limb (b) is not met; and your own device sat between 690 m and 717 m from the pickup pin for the entire window, with no qualifying fix inside the 150 m rider-presence radius, so limb (c) fails affirmatively. POL-NS-03 does not apply either: the pickup has a single registered point (so pin ambiguity is unavailable) and the driver's holds were inside the arrival zone, not at a wrong face of the building.

DRIVER — your account matches the record: you were at the bay, the advisory explains why you had to leave the kerb, and you were back within about 120 seconds. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so POL-NS-07 pays you 80% of the $4.00 fee, i.e. $3.20, the remaining $0.80 being retained as the platform service fee. On a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling the amount field carries that same $3.20; it is not a refund to the rider, whose $4.00 charge stands. The anti-farming guard does not bite: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days (threshold 4) and a rate of 2/118 = 1.7% (threshold 8%).

No artifact is impaired: the trace has 100% coverage with no gap in the waiting window, the chat is complete and matches the trip record's message count, the fare reconciles with the fee schedule (greater of the $4.00 zone fee and the $4.00 tier fee), and the driver's track is intact. The case is therefore decided at full weight, confidence is above the 0.70 floor, and no escalation or referral is required.

ledger.claim: The driver never held the pickup point for the minimum waiting period in any continuous stretch. On his own trace the two spells inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup are 170 seconds (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 seconds (18:49:35 to 18:52:40), against the 300 second minimum for the zone class. His longest single hold is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short, and neither spell reaches five minutes. That is exactly the rider's complaint, in her own words, that the car never stayed five minutes in one place before the driver cancelled and charged her SGD 4.00.

The charge also fails POL-NS-01(d), which makes the fee chargeable only where the trip is terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. Measured from the start of the driver's final in-geofence hold at 18:49:35, a continuous 300 second dwell would not have elapsed until 18:54:35, yet the trip record shows the driver cancelling at 18:52:45 - 110 seconds early. The cancellation therefore lands inside the waiting period the fee is supposed to purchase, not after it.

POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) both run off the trace, not off the driver's tap. Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 pickup geofence at or before the 18:44:30 'arrived' event, and limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the event. The trace's in-geofence intervals begin only at 18:44:45, fifteen seconds after the marker, so the record does not establish an in-geofence position at the moment the driver marked arrived, and the waiting clock cannot be started earlier than 18:44:45 on this evidence.

The only route to 300 seconds on this record is the summing allowed by POL-NS-06(i). The kerb-restriction advisory on the file does one thing: it permits the two in-geofence spells to be added together. It does not convert the 120 seconds the car spent away from the bay - 18:47:35 to 18:49:35, when the driver's own trace puts the vehicle up to 179 m from the pin - into waiting time, and the driver's own chat message at 18:47:50 ('i go one round and come back same place ah') is his admission that he left. Even taking the accumulated figure at its highest, the driver clears the 300 second minimum by only 55 seconds, on a trace whose longest undisturbed hold is 185 seconds. The rider is asked to pay for a continuous wait that was never held.

POL-NS-06 is strict about the waiting period: where the effective dwell falls short, the fee is refunded to the rider in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The driver's account that the rider said she was coming down at 6.46 and never came cannot therefore save the charge - the fee is earned by the dwell, not by the rider's conduct - and the contested SGD 4.00 should be returned in full to the filing rider under POL-GEN-03.

The driver's own trace contains 40 qualifying position fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius fixed for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, delivered as two continuous in-geofence holds of 18 fixes (18:44:45-18:47:35) and 20 fixes (18:49:35-18:52:40). POL-NS-02 requires only three consecutive in-radius fixes with 25 m accuracy or better, so the driver is deemed to have ARRIVED at the ION Orchard PHV bay on the platform's own numbers, not on his say-so.

The rider's core complaint is that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place.' That is true of the longest single hold (185 seconds), and it is precisely the case POL-NS-06(i) was written for: dwell may be accumulated across separate in-geofence intervals where the driver never went more than 300 m from the pin AND a traffic advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION covered the pickup road during the waiting period. Here the LTA advisory is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane 17:00-20:00 on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn between Paterson Rd and Bideford Rd), its geometry contains the pickup point and its window covers the whole wait, and the driver's furthest point during the loop was 179.0 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. The effective dwell is therefore 170 + 185 = 355 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum, the derived shortfall is negative (-55 s), and POL-NS-06's full-refund route is not triggered.

The chat independently corroborates the loop and its cause. At 18:47:50 — exactly when the trace shows the driver leaving the bay at 18:47:35 to begin the 120 second excursion — he wrote 'boss the marshal make me move, bus lane until 8pm. i go one round and come back same place ah'. The trace shows him back at the same bay by 18:49:35. The absence from the kerb was compliance with a lawfully enforced bus lane, not abandonment of the pickup, which is the situation POL-NS-06(i) exists to stop penalising.

All four POL-NS-01 limbs are made out on this record. (a) The trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30. (b) The trace places the driver in the pickup geofence with 40 qualifying fixes. (c) The effective in-geofence dwell under POL-NS-06(i) is 355 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the 'arrived' tap. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, no boarding event and no started_at. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces that, so the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is chargeable as itemised.

Taking the point against the driver at its highest — that the 18:44:30 'arrived' tap preceded the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45 by 15 seconds — POL-NS-05 still does not defeat the fee. Its trigger is a fix more than 300 m from the pin or travel at 15 km/h or above at the marker; more importantly limb (iii) says expressly that a marker which is merely early is not a technicality that voids an otherwise good fee, because the waiting clock is simply recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and on that recomputed basis the dwell (355 seconds accumulated) still meets the LARGE_VENUE minimum. POL-NS-01 therefore governs the outcome.

POL-NS-04 cannot exculpate the rider on either limb. Limb (b) fails: the rider's only message in the waiting window is MSG-00214-003 at 18:46:20 ('ok coming down now'), and the driver answered it in the chat at 18:47:50 — 90 seconds later, inside the 120 second limit — so the no-reply condition is not met and the clause does not apply. Limb (c) fails affirmatively as well: the rider_track records 70 fixes, every one of them outside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider presence radius (minimum 690.7 m, mean 702.7 m from the pin), giving rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0.

The rider's narrative — 'I was watching the app the whole time' and 'coming down now' — is contradicted by his own device. His track runs 70 fixes from 18:44:00 to 18:52:40, all at 0.0 km/h, pinned between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin for the entire window. At 18:46:20 he told the driver he was coming down; six minutes later he had moved not at all. That is the RIDER_NO_SHOW cancellation reason code made out on the rider's own telemetry, and it is why the fee was charged.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 gives the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, with the 20 percent platform service fee retained. The anti-farming guard does not bite: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, far below 0.08. Both limbs are required and neither is met, so compensation is payable and no escalation arises under POL-NS-09.

The amount charged is correct and gives the rider no route to even a partial refund. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) — and the two dimensions agree, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and there is no fare defect for the rider to exploit.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius; this driver's holds were inside it, so there is no wrong-entrance or wrong-block case to allocate. Its pin-ambiguity branch in limb (ii) is unavailable in any event because trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more, so no platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent arises and the fee is not displaced.
